result.title: Understanding and Repairing Cooperative Perception under Adverse Weather
result.summary: A cooperative 3D detector can miss a vehicle even when the LiDAR points on it remain unchanged. We study this failure under adverse weather as Weather-Induced Context Interference. To our knowledge, this is the first controlled study of how weather-related exterior changes remove cooperative benefits while preserving all points inside annotated objects. Controlled experiments on simulated and real roadside inputs show that exterior loss changes object representations before fusion and removes previously useful assistance. On real inputs, restoring object-neighborhood features recovers 30 of 31 induced failures; three equal-area exterior controls recover none. The failure condition also appears with a second fusion model. These findings motivate Adverse-Weather Cooperative Repair (AWCR), with separate implementations for the available supervision. Point Classifier filters added weather returns in simulation. On real inputs, Local Correction refines candidates and Quality Selection checks them against current measurements, without naturally paired clear/adverse-weather recordings. Candidate tracing shows that correction supplies accurate geometry for some targets that original candidates cannot localize at the evaluation threshold. On natural adverse-weather CoInfra development data, AWCR improves car bird's-eye-view (BEV) AP@0.7 by 4.66 points with V2X-ViT and 5.56 with AttFuse. On simulated V2X-R fog, it improves vehicle BEV AP@0.7 by 4.47 points at a fixed 4,096-candidate budget.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究恶劣天气下协同3D检测的「天气诱导上下文干扰」：在目标内部点云不变时，目标外部特征变化会在融合前改变目标表征并消除协同收益，并提出 AWCR（点分类器过滤、局部校正与质量选择）来修复。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「移除/恢复目标邻域特征」的受控干预定位到表征层面失效来源，配合候选校正与质量筛选，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索，但属于点云协同检测，迁移需较多核查。
